summary: All three TDD anchors are present and behavioral (write-then-read, invalidate clears, injected suite leaves .standard untouched). Each passes the litmus test: removing the corresponding OrgIDStore method body would fail its test. Suites are isolated (unique UUID-based suiteName), guarded with #require, and torn down via removePersistentDomain in a defer. Idiom matches QuotaParserTests (struct test type, import Testing, @Test, #expect). Assertions are meaningful (no mock-only or tautological checks). The only gaps are three of the task's explicitly enumerated edge cases that lack dedicated tests; none are high/critical, so this approves.

findings.gap: Edge case 'reading when nothing has been cached -> nil' is not directly tested. invalidateClearsUUID reaches a nil read, but only via write+invalidate, which exercises removeObject, not the fresh/never-written path. A brand-new store reading nil is a distinct branch (string(forKey:) on an empty suite).
findings.suggestion: Add @Test func readOnEmptyStoreReturnsNil() that constructs the store via withIsolatedStore and asserts #expect(store.read() == nil) with no prior write.

findings.gap: Edge case 'invalidating when nothing is cached -> no-op, no crash' is not tested. invalidate() is only ever called after a write, so the empty-invalidate path (removeObject on absent key) is unguarded.
findings.suggestion: Add @Test func invalidateOnEmptyStoreIsNoOp() that calls store.invalidate() on a fresh store and asserts #expect(store.read() == nil) (test passing without throwing also proves no crash).

findings.gap: Edge case 'overwriting an existing UUID -> new value replaces old' is not tested, even though the write() doc-comment claims it 'replac[es] any previous value'. No test guards the overwrite semantics.
findings.suggestion: Add @Test func writeOverwritesPreviousValue() that writes uuidA, then writes uuidB, and asserts #expect(store.read() == uuidB).

findings.gap: withIsolatedStore passes a second closure argument (suiteName) to every test body, but no test uses it. Dead parameter adds noise versus the QuotaParserTests idiom of minimal setup.
findings.suggestion: Drop the unused String from the closure signature: private func withIsolatedStore(_ body: (OrgIDStore) throws -> Void) throws, simplifying all three call sites.
